OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner. The value is normalized to
            E.164 form. Spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped. A leading '+' and country
            code are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single
            leading '0' is dropped from the national digits. The result must be a '+'
            followed by 8 to 15 digits. For example '0412 345 678' is stored as '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[-0-9()+.\s]*$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: The owner's 4-digit postcode. Optional. When present it must be valid
            for the owner's city per the fixed region ranges (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099,
            QLD 4000-4099); a city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored
            and returned when supplied.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered. When omitted on create it
            defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: The pet owner's date of birth. Optional. When present it is used to
            derive the owner's ageBand against the registrationDate. Accepted and returned
            in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: When true, declares this owner a deliberate member of an existing
            household and bypasses the household duplicate block, allowing creation even though
            another owner already shares the same lastName and postcode (the household key).
            Otherwise such a request is rejected with 409 Conflict. A declared member is created
            and is not flagged as a possible duplicate.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true

Done. The refactor compiles and the test suite is in exactly the same state as before my change: same 1 pass / 1 fail, no regression.

## What I did

I prepared the create-owner intake pipeline so the upcoming structured-address change has a natural home, without implementing the change itself.

**The seam I created** — `OwnerRestControllerV1.applyAddress(OwnerFieldsDto)`:

`prepareNewOwner` reads as a clean list of named intake steps (`validateRequiredFields`, `validatePostcode`, `rejectDuplicateIdentity`, …) — every step is its own method *except* address handling, which was the one inlined line:

```java
ownerFieldsDto.setAddress(normalizeAddress(ownerFieldsDto.getAddress()));
```

That inlined step is exactly where the change piles on complexity (prefer structured `addressLine1`/`addressLine2` fields, normalize whichever are supplied, compose the returned `address`). I extracted it into a dedicated `applyAddress` step-method (matching the house style, verbose javadoc and all), so `prepareNewOwner` stays a list of named steps and address handling has one place to grow.

Behavior is byte-for-byte identical: `applyAddress` still just delegates to `normalizeAddress` and writes back in place, ahead of the required-field check.

## Why nothing else was touched

The other listed hotspots are the *footprint* of the future change, and touching them now would either change behavior or implement the feature:

- **`Owner.getAddressLine1/2` / `setAddressLine1/2`** — these fields don't exist yet. Adding them (plus the composed-`address` logic) requires the DTO/OpenAPI schema and mapper wiring that *is* the feature. Adding entity columns with no wiring would also be dead code and risks the JPA schema.
- **`updateOwner`** — it currently sets `address` *raw* (no normalization), unlike the create path. The change deliberately alters this ("This changes existing behaviour"). Any seam I'd introduce there would either change behavior now or presuppose the feature, so I left it exactly as-is.

## One thing to flag about the tests

The repo already contains the feature's acceptance oracle, `AcceptanceTest.coreNormalizesAndComposesStructuredAddress`, and it was **already failing before I started** — it asserts the not-yet-built structured-address behavior. Since the instruction is to prepare *without* implementing the change, I kept that test red (making it green would mean implementing the feature) and confirmed the previously-passing `functionalityStillAcceptsFlatAddress` still passes. When the real change lands in `applyAddress`, that oracle should flip to green.
